subject: Future Tech
title: Mutations: Nature's Editor
description: Learn Mutations: Nature's Editor in one minute.

hook.text: Every time a cell divides, it copies 3.2 billion DNA letters. Mistakes happen, and those mistakes are called mutations.

buildup.text: Most mutations are harmless. Some are deadly. A few are beneficial and drive evolution by giving organisms new traits.

discovery.text: Sickle cell disease comes from a single letter change in one gene.

twist.text: Carrying one copy of the sickle cell mutation protects against malaria.

climax.text: Gene editing aims to fix harmful mutations while leaving the rest of the genome untouched. Surgery at the letter level.

punchline.text: One wrong letter in three billion can change everything.
